about: A change says when it may have reformatted rows its Rows does not name (ADR-0071, ticket 48): a whole row's or column's Cell Format is shown by the cells that hold nothing as well, and rows or columns inserted or deleted bring two cells' sides together on a new edge. Transcribed from ExSheet.Engine.Tests' UnnamedRowsTests.

cases.name: ADR-0071, ticket 48: a Fill on a whole column of empty cells names no row, and says it reformatted rows
ADR-0071, ticket 48: bold on whole rows names only the rows that hold a cell, and reaches the others
ADR-0071, ticket 48: undoing and redoing a level change reaches unnamed rows too
ADR-0071, ticket 48: a level change among several ranges reaches unnamed rows
ADR-0071, ticket 48: a level set to what it already shows changes nothing, and reaches nothing
ADR-0071, ticket 48: a Cell Format on cells names their rows and the rows across their edges, and nothing beyond
ADR-0071, ticket 48: an entry reaches no row it does not name
ADR-0071, ticket 48: inserting or deleting rows or columns brings sides together on new edges, so it reaches unnamed rows: insert rows
ADR-0071, ticket 48: inserting or deleting rows or columns brings sides together on new edges, so it reaches unnamed rows: delete rows
ADR-0071, ticket 48: inserting or deleting rows or columns brings sides together on new edges, so it reaches unnamed rows: insert columns
ADR-0071, ticket 48: inserting or deleting rows or columns brings sides together on new edges, so it reaches unnamed rows: delete columns
ADR-0071, ticket 48: deleting the row between two edges changes the line an empty row shows, which Rows does not name

steps.note: A2's top was the edge A1 shows as its bottom; A1 holds nothing.
